newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says Spain breaks single market rules.
newsitem.headline: EU says Spain breaks single market rules.

text.p: Spain will be taken to the European Court of Justice for obstructing free trade rules within the 15-nation bloc regarding the setting up of private security firms, the European Commission said on Monday.
Belgium, Italy and Germany must also change their rules in other sectors, it added.

Under a Spanish law of July, 1992, companies providing services such as security guards, private detectives and transport of valuables, must be provided by Spanish companies and staff must also be Spanish.
"The Commission considers this situation to be an infringement of EC Treaty rules," it said in a statement.
It said it had explained to Madrid its view that Spanish law infringes EU rules on the freedom of setting up businesses, the freedom to provide services and the free movement of workers.
But Spain replied in September that it refused to change its rules.
"The Commission has therefore decided to refer Spain to the Court of Justice," the EU's executive said, referring to the Luxembourg-based court.
Germany was told that rules allowing only German firms to use Polish sub-contractors in the construction industry broke the EU principle of cross-border freedom to provide services.
Belgium was told that rules requiring international charities, religious and other non-profit making associations to have Belgian associates were discriminatory and broke EU rules.
Italy was told that restrictions on the organisation of trade fair and exhibitions broke EU rules on the right of establishment.
But the Commission said it was dropping legal action against Luxembourg after it changed rules for companies inspecting work places.
